why: ONE rule for which running process is a Kimi (DL10 of research/PLAN_kimi_and_vibe_on_linux.md): a listing reads a process's NAME from the basename of its /proc/<pid>/exe link
(one trailing ' (deleted)' taken off), or - when the exe is hidden - from the basename of argv[0] (nothing is taken off argv[0]); the process is a Kimi when that name is 'kimi' or
'kimi.exe' in any case, OR its comm is exactly 'kimi' (case-sensitive). A comm of 'MainThread' alone is not Kimi - a running `kimi acp` has it, and its exe is the witness.
Both halves read this file and assert their own code against it: the product (ForeignKimiWatch.IsKimi over LinuxProcessListing, KimiIdentityVectorTests in src_mcp/tests) and the
probes (isKimi over linuxProcesses, scripts/lib/proc.test.mjs). A change to one side's rule turns only that side red; a change here turns both.
exe: the /proc/<pid>/exe target, or null when the exe is hidden (EACCES); argv: the cmdline arguments, read only when exe is null; comm: the stat comm.
name: what the listing reads; isKimi: the answer.
